title: Recursive supported-dependency discovery
description:
Implement recursive discovery for supported local bundle dependencies of working-tree artifacts: Markdown and HTML element URLs, including script `src`, plus CSS `@import` and `url()`. Resolve paths by normalized components, distinguish relative and root-relative edges, reject repository escape, detect cycles, and retain enough edge data for before/after reachability validation. Detect the binding dynamic-loading pattern set textually — `fetch(`, `import(`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `new Worker(`, `importScripts(`, URL-bearing `data-*` attributes, and static module syntax with relative specifiers (`import`/`export ... from`/`require`) — and report matches in relocated members as warnings, never blocking and never executing or guessing JavaScript: the pattern set cannot distinguish live loaders from code examples in presentation content. Pinned roots contribute no embedded-closure scan; a pinned root whose commit read fails blocks the target, and a readable pinned root imposes no working-tree constraint. Existing snapshot-export callers remain unchanged because this is a new recursive path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Discovery reaches an HTML to sibling CSS to nested figure chain and recursively follows CSS `@import` and `url()` targets; script-element `src` is a supported static edge.
- [hard] REQ-02: Cycles terminate deterministically, repository escapes are rejected, and local-path-bearing constructs from the complete binding dynamic-loading set produce the `dynamic-loading-suspected` warning by textual matching only, without blocking the target.
- [hard] REQ-03: A pinned root whose commit read fails produces `pinned-read-failed` with no working-tree fallback; a readable pinned root yields a non-relocating historical entry with no embedded-closure scan and no working-tree constraint.
